failure_summary.description: Several calls passed display labels or noncanonical values where the endpoint expected a code, slug, token, normalized value, or different value encoding.
Some trajectories split facets across overlapping tools, added an unrequested call, or failed to use the endpoint that matched the requested operation.
Some arguments were put in the wrong required/optional group, output fields were omitted, or values did not follow the expected serialization convention.

patch.reasoning: The batch repeatedly shows confusion between user-facing labels and endpoint-specific parameter representations, so the value-mapping rule should make that decision more operational. A second recurring issue is splitting multiple checks for one target even when one endpoint explicitly covers them all; clarifying the existing broad-endpoint rule addresses this without adding a general fan-out rule. Schema grouping and serialization guidance is already explicit in the skill, so it does not need another edit.

edits.target: For a broad request, prefer a documented broad or all-scope endpoint when it fully provides the requested output; do not choose a narrower endpoint merely because it has fewer required arguments. Conversely, cover separately requested outputs when they require distinct endpoints rather than assuming one broad or multi-capability lookup covers every facet.
edits.content: For multiple facets on the same target, first check whether one documented endpoint explicitly satisfies them all; if so, use it once rather than combining narrower or alternative checks. Otherwise, cover separately requested outputs with distinct endpoints rather than assuming one broad or multi-capability lookup covers every facet. Prefer the broadest documented endpoint that fulfills the request without sacrificing its scope.

edits.target: Preserve query values and their entity associations, converting them only to documented formats such as API codes, list syntax, or canonical enum spelling. Match the representation expected by each field: use a canonical slug when the schema requires one and convert quantities to documented units (for example, 5 minutes to 300 seconds).
edits.content: Preserve query values and their entity associations, but treat the field schema and endpoint documentation as authoritative about representation. Before passing a user-facing label, check whether the field expects a canonical code, slug, enum token, normalized case, marketplace identifier, list syntax, or converted unit; map to that form only when a documented mapping, reference endpoint, or standard unambiguous API convention establishes it. Do not put display text into a code/slug/token field or guess an opaque value. When a field accepts free text and no canonical representation is specified, retain the user's value.
